newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Ecopetrol says no word yet on Colombia oil exports.
newsitem.headline: Ecopetrol says no word yet on Colombia oil exports.

text.p: Colombia's state-run oil company Ecopetrol said late Monday it had still not decided whether to declare force majeure on crude exports.

Ecopetrol declared force majeure on the transport of crude along the Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline earlier in the day after a series of back-to-back rebel dynamite attacks and a landslide ruptured the pipe in three places at the weekend.
"There is still no word on the export situation. Force majeure (for exports) is still under consideration," the spokesman said.
Occidental Petroleum Corp declared force majeure on production at the Cano Limon field it operates in northeast Colombia but refrained from extending the move to its exports.
Storage tanks at the lifting terminal on the Caribbean coast at Covenas have capacity for about 2 million barrels but Ecopetrol declined to say whether or not they were full.
The spokesman also refused to say what the deliveries and liftings schedule was over the next few days.
The force majeure -- a legal move which allows the pipeline and field operators to temporarily suspend contracts and obligations without penalty -- is the second in three weeks.
The last one in mid-July also affected exports and remained in force for about one week.

Ecopetrol said it would take until at least Friday to repair the pipeline. Pumping has been suspended since last Wednesday after an earlier dynamite attack by rebels of the national Liberation Army (ELN), the country's second largest guerrilla force.
